coordinate_space: Position space, X right / Y down, origin at the feet/action anchor; per-frame pivot_px is that anchor inside the cell (uv top-left relative, y down)

anchor_convention.basis: taubeast body frames share position [-320,-500] => anchor at canvas (320,500), ground contact (position-space bottom of the sprite) ~+20 px below the anchor; overturn shifts position to [-320,-228] like the goblin's flipped-on-back frame. Same per-frame anchor convention as goblinthrower (see its config basis); charge/warning effect frames likewise carry their own positions [-164,-343]/[-164,-327]/[-40,-32].
anchor_convention.evidence: verify monster_taubeast.json animations[*].frames[*].position; behavior_mapping 'charge1/charge2/fullcharge1 contain zero body frames - they are pure effect overlays'
anchor_convention.note: untransformed frames place the layer canvas at the frame position exactly like M8-016; transforms apply about the per-frame anchor, which always lands at position-space (0,0)

transform_semantics.rotation_direction: positive degrees rotate counterclockwise in y-down image space (PIL rotate(+angle), anchor at image center)
transform_semantics.scale_rule: content resized about the anchor, half-up rounding, NEAREST; the anchor offset rounds identically so the anchor lands exactly on the canvas anchor; outer edges may drift <= 1 px from the ideal float position
transform_semantics.color_rule: per-frame color_rgba multiplies RGBA channels (c_out = c_src*color/255); baked into the cell and recorded per frame

layer_rule.note: monsters have no outfit layers; each frame references exactly one image (body atlas or class effect overlay). taubeast charge/warning actions are pure effect overlays (verify external_deps): their cells carry the effect art at the authored frame scale; sorting_layer below the body (5 vs 10) is recorded per action for runtime draw ordering
